title: Harden the canonical direct-port 4x4 segmented mesh
hypothesis: Hardening the exact functional mesh hierarchy will remove synthetic harness logic from aggregate NoC PPA and provide a routed hierarchy that can accept verified Llama7B endpoint activity.

direct_comparison.primary_question: What PPA does the complete functional sixteen-router mesh consume relative to the compact synthetic aggregate harness?
include: all functional endpoint ready/valid and flit ports
aggregate clock tree and routed-wire effects

expected_benefit: separate functional mesh cost from synthetic harness overhead
measure aggregate links and clock distribution in the exact hierarchy
enable hierarchy-matched post-route Llama7B transport energy
risks: the 8962 functional pins can still constrain perimeter placement
the first point is a loose feasibility envelope rather than die optimization
the sixteen-router hierarchy may cross the Yosys/OpenROAD runtime frontier
vectorless power does not represent workload energy

required_evaluations.objective: Measure Nangate45 PPA for the canonical direct-port sixteen-router segmented mesh without synthetic harness logic.

expected_result.reason: The compact aggregate target cannot accept endpoint workload activity and includes synthetic boundary logic.

required_evaluations.acceptance_notes: Require canonical source identity, a logic-free functional wrapper, all sixteen routers, the explicit 8962-pin perimeter gate, complete PPA, timing feasibility, retained routed artifacts, and isolated flow identity. Debug-counter pins, endpoints/SRAM, and HBM/DRAM remain excluded.
